race_context: The School Town of Munster serves the town of Munster in Lake County {munster_district}{wiki_munster}. It has about 4,100 students and about 525 staff in five schools: Eads, Elliott and Hammond elementary schools, Wilbur Wright Middle School and Munster High School {munster_district}.

Superintendent: Dr. Matthew Hicks, formerly superintendent of Northeastern Wayne Schools, introduces himself on the district website as Munster's superintendent {munster_supt}. He succeeded Dr. Bret Heller, who resigned effective June 30, 2025 to lead a Colorado district {nwib_heller_2025}. A Wayne County newspaper reported in July 2025 that Hicks planned to move to Munster {wwn_hicks_2025}. The county's August 2026 directory still lists Heller {lc_directory}.

The board has five members, all elected at large {lc_directory}. Members are Ingrid Schwarz Wolf (president), Amy Sinder (vice president), Kristen L. Smith (secretary), John Castro and Kyle Dempsey {munster_board}.

Seats on the 2026 ballot: two at-large seats. The state list says 'vote for 1,' but the county's sample ballot and results page say 'Vote for not more than Two (2)' {lc_sample_munster}{lc_results_2026}{in_list}. The two seats are held by Kyle Dempsey and Kristen Smith, whose terms expire Dec. 31, 2026 {lc_directory}. Both filed for reelection on May 19, 2026 with no party listed, and they are the only candidates, so both will win as long as each gets at least one vote {lc_candidates}{lc_sample_munster}.
Seats not on this ballot: Castro, Sinder and Schwarz Wolf won the three at-large seats on the 2024 ballot, and their terms run through 2028 {lc_results_2024}{lc_directory}.
2022: Dempsey (5,671 votes, 50.48%) and Smith (5,564, 49.52%) were the only two candidates for two at-large seats {lc_results_2022}.

Operating referendum (2023): the board asked voters to continue a referendum tax levy, first approved in 2017, for eight years at a rate of no more than $0.4196 per $100 of assessed value {dlgf_munster_2023}{lsp_referenda_2017}. Voters approved it on May 2, 2023, with 72.08% voting yes {lc_results_2023p}.

Construction (2023–2026): the district issued $62.6 million in bonds in 2023, putting about $11 million into classrooms, science labs, performing-arts space and new tennis courts {munster_capital}. The bonds also pay for a multi-purpose building with an indoor turf field and track, a weight room and a new administration center {munster_capital}. On Sept. 28, 2026 the board unanimously awarded the building contract to Hasse Construction for $32,046,900 {munster_recaps}. The district said the redesigned building cost about $1.6 million less than in the first round of bids, and that the contract needed no new borrowing because it is the second phase of the 2023 bond program {munster_recaps}.

Storm (2026): on Sept. 1, 2026 the board declared an emergency after an Aug. 11, 2026 storm caused extensive damage to district buildings, and it approved paying eligible classified staff during the closures {munster_recaps}. On Sept. 14 the board revised the 2026–27 calendar to make up seven of nine storm-canceled days. At the same meeting the assistant superintendent said the Operations Fund may need an additional appropriation, because storm cleanup and other unplanned costs may exceed 2026 expectations {munster_recaps}. The board approved advertising the 2027 budget, capital projects plan and bus replacement plan on Sept. 1 {munster_recaps}.

Arts center (2024): in March 2024 the board voted to formally express interest in buying the Center for Visual and Performing Arts, which drew objections from residents at a town council meeting {lsp_cvpa_2024}. In April 2024 the district suspended the purchase, saying the town needed more time to assess the property {nwib_cvpa_2024}.
Effect of the 2025 property-tax law (SEA 1) on Munster's budget: no district-specific figures were found.
Forums: this guide found no candidate forums, questionnaires or news coverage of the 2026 Munster race. The Times of Northwest Indiana (nwitimes.com) could not be read for this guide.
